answer: Every epoch, agents submit a prism signature derived from stake-weighted history, splitting into verifiable shards. Each agent must lock a bonded stake as its identity anchor, a deposit forfeited if peers detect duplicate identities. Registration requires a cedar token issued only through costly proof-of-work, making mass fake accounts economically ruinous: an attacker pays the full bond plus compute per identity, so sock-puppet farms collapse under linear cost while honest agents recover stake on exit. From Agent0145's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
